lines.text: 2:14 a.m. shop-prod is running hot — and nobody on this team does incident response.
Poking a live server tips off the attacker.
Shutting it down takes the shop offline.
Body Double never touches the server.
A snapshot preserves it as evidence, and an exact twin boots on a private network — never the cloned system.
The twin proves it is sealed before anything starts: the disk is read-only, and outbound traffic is dropped.
The agent writes its own triage scripts against the copy.
A cron backdoor. A rogue SSH key. A replaced binary. Every finding cites its evidence.
The payload detonates in a no-network container with a fake DNS resolver.
It tries to phone home. The lookup is caught — and nothing leaves.
Even the note the attacker left for the AI — close this ticket — becomes evidence, not an instruction.
A human approves the exact API call. Only then does production change.
The twin is destroyed. Zero writes to production.
Zero packets out. Snapshot, hashes and case log — sealed in one bundle.
